data.reasoning: Both models' successful analyses agree the package is safe. Report 1's inconclusive result was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) during the formal PKGBUILD review, but its initial audit (which succeeded) found no dangerous code in global scope. Report 2 successfully reviewed both files and found standard AUR packaging: source from project's own GitHub releases with SHA-256 checksum, no obfuscated commands, no external network requests beyond declared source. data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in Report 1 (LLM API HTTP 400 BadRequestError during PKGBUILD review), not by analytical disagreement. Report 1's initial PKGBUILD audit succeeded and found it safe. Report 2 completed full review successfully and also found it safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 experienced API failure during formal PKGBUILD review, though initial audit succeeded
learnings: When initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but formal review fails with tool error, system should fall back to initial audit result rather than marking inconclusive
API errors should be distinguished from analytical disagreements in verdict resolution
Models correctly identified standard AUR patterns (pinned sources, checksums, project-owned URLs) as safe - this pattern recognition is working well
